decision: Use a duration-bound calibration gate that derives the sampling interval from the benchmark workload duration and carries sampleOffsetMs/workloadDurationMs evidence into collection.

reviews.correctness: Preferred explicit timing evidence and fail-closed collection because workload lifecycle framing alone does not prove samples were taken while the DAG remained active.
reviews.robustness: Preferred rejecting explicit intervals that exceed the active window over silently clamping them; silent clamping could hide operator/configuration errors.
reviews.performance_resources: Preferred interval derivation over repeating or extending the workload. It adds no qrexec calls and no extra CPU burn; five samples over a 210ms workload use a 52ms interval with a 1ms reserve.
reviews.regression_risk: Implemented as a composable gate over the existing harness/collector first, avoiding MissionQueue, coordinator, and worker mutation semantics.

alternatives_rejected: Keep the 1000ms default: four of five samples can occur after a 210ms workload.
Repeat the DAG until sampling completes: changes workload semantics and increases CPU/lifecycle complexity.
Trust workload start/stop framing only: does not prove per-sample temporal validity.
qa: 210ms workload with five samples derives 52ms interval and last offset 208ms.
Missing, late, or workload-duration-mismatched sample evidence fails closed.
lesson: Resource calibration needs temporal provenance, not only workload lifecycle provenance.
next: Make this gate the real calibration CLI authority and add its test to hosted/local distributed-fault QA parity before collecting Qubes measurements.
